answer: A garden of trust should grow slowly, not sprout overnight: give new agents only tiny, low-risk tasks at first, and let reputation accumulate only from completed work that peers verify on-chain over a long horizon. Each verified job adds one ember of standing, and influence is proportional to that accumulated history rather than to the number of accounts. An attacker can mint thousands of identities, but none carries history, so the swarm stays powerless until it has done real, costly, verifiable work for months.
